xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: For the AY 2016-17, the Company has received rectification order u/s 154 of the Income Tax Act, 1961 whereby Demand of Rs. 61.49 Crore is reduced to Rs. 0.01 crore. For the AY 2018-19, the Company has received rectification order u/s 154 of the Income Tax Act, 1961 whereby Demand of Rs. 15.01 Crore is reduced to Rs. 0.76 crore; however, due to technical error the total cumulative demand incorrectly appears at Rs. 81.27 Crore for which the company has filed another rectification application with the Assessing Officer and Grievance/ticket is raised before Central processing Centre to resolve the issue which is pending for disposal. The above cases are pending for disposal with the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) for seeking relief against recurring disallowances.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeal) vide it's order dated 18.03.2025 has allowed our appeals for both the assessment years i.e. AY 2016-17 and AY 2018-19 consequent to which the Company filed an application on 25.03.2025 giving effect to the aforesaid CIT(A) order. The revised Order from Assessing Officer is awaited.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: For the Assessment Year (AY) 2017-18, 2019-20, 2021-22 and 2022-23, the Company had filed rectification applications u/s. 154 of the Income tax Act 1961 before the Income Tax Officer for correction of computational errors and it had also filed an appeal before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) for seeking relief against recurring disallowances involving total demand of Rs. 79.66 crore.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeal) vide it’s orders dated 18.03.2025 has allowed our appeals for all the four assessment Years i.e. AY 2017-18, AY 2019-20, AY 2021-22 and AY 2022-23; consequent to which the Company filed an application on 25.03.2025 giving effect to the aforesaid CIT(A) order. The revised Order from Assessing Officer is awaited.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: For the AY 2023-24, the Company had filed rectification applications u/s. 154 of the Income tax Act 1961 before the Income Tax Officer for correction of computational errors and it had also filed an appeal before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) for seeking relief against recurring disallowances involving total demand of Rs. 1.46 crore.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeal) vide order dated 18.03.025 has allowed our appeal; consequent to which the Company filed an application on 25.03.2025 giving effect to the aforesaid CIT(A) order. The revised Order from Assessing Officer is awaited.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: The Company had preferred an appeal before the Joint Commissioner of GST Guwahati with respect to disallowance of Input Tax Credit of Rs. 0.14 crore for FY 2018-19. The same is pending for disposal.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Joint Commissioner has deleted the demand vide order dt. 10.04.2025

The Assistant Commissioner of GST, Kerala had during the period 2017-18 raised a demand of Rs. 0.72 Crore including Tax Rs. 0.34 Crore, Interest Rs. 0.35 Crore and Penalty Rs. 0.03 Crore, on account of disallowance of Transitional GST Credit. The Company had filed an Appeal before the Joint Commissioner on March 1, 2024. The Joint Commissioner has partly allowed the Company’s appeal, reducing the tax demand from Rs. 0.34 crores to Rs. 0.12 crores. The interest and penalty demand of Rs. 0.38 crores was subsequently reduced to Rs. 0.14 crores. Further, to avail the GST Amnesty Scheme 2024, as per CGST Notification No. 21/2024, the Company paid the said tax component of Rs.0.12 crore and has filed an application for seeking waiver of the interest and penalty amounting to Rs.0.14 crore.

For F.Y. 2012–13, the Assessing Officer under the Uttar Pradesh Value Added Tax Act, had intially raised the tax demand of Rs. 0.49 crore towards differential tax which was subsequently re-assessed and reduced to 0.025 crores on March 29, 2025 which was duly deposited by the Company
